hook.text: When a guitar string vibrates four hundred forty times per second, you hear concert pitch.

buildup.text: The number of vibrations per second is called frequency, measured in a unit called hertz.

discovery.text: Higher frequency means higher pitch, which is why a piccolo sounds shriller than a bass drum.

twist.text: Doubling the frequency raises a note by exactly one octave, a relationship found across all music.

climax.text: Producers use frequency knowledge to place instruments in the right range and avoid clashes.

punchline.text: Pitch is just how fast the air vibrates.

quiz.question: What happens when you double a sound's frequency?
